body: American Hospitality Properties REIT, Inc. and 15 affiliates, including American Hospitality Properties REIT II, Inc., filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on October 4, 2026 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Texas, WhatNow reported, citing PACER records. The affiliates include a master-lease entity and hotel-owning entities in locations including Cape Canaveral, Bentonville, Baton Rouge, Fayetteville, Fort Myers, Jonesboro, Metairie and Charlotte. The REITs own hotels operated under Marriott and Hilton brands; WhatNow noted the petition does not indicate that either hotel company owns the REIT. The case, No. 26-80071, is assigned to Judge Stacey G.C. Jernigan.

According to WhatNow, the board approved the filing after reviewing the company's financial condition, liquidity and obligations. The chief restructuring officer signed the petition, and Vinson & Elkins LLP and FTI Consulting were retained as counsel and financial advisor. The petition lists estimated liabilities of $1,000,001 to $10 million and estimated assets of $0 to $50,000. Its largest unsecured creditors include Marriott International, Inc. (about $1.94 million in franchise fees), Hilton Hotels Corporation (about $191,364 in franchise fees), PAH Management (management fees), Spirit Realty LP (ground rent) and Deutsche Bank AG (a bank loan).

Phoenix American Hospitality, LLC (PAH) was the external manager of both REITs until the REITs ended their management agreements effective May 20, 2026, according to SEC filings cited by WhatNow. On June 4, 2026, the SEC filed a settled action against PAH and its president in federal court in Dallas; the court entered judgments the next day, the docket shows. The SEC alleged the two raised about $86 million from more than 2,000 retail investors between March 2022 and July 2024 through two hotel funds, that neither fund was profitable despite claimed distributions of up to 12%, and that investors were told REIT I had acquired about 11 hotels when it held one until January 2024. Without admitting or denying the claims, PAH agreed to pay $591,127 and Nelson $118,225, and Nelson agreed to a five-year officer-and-director bar.

On September 15, 2026, Proven Business Skills Inc filed suit against PAH in the same federal court (No. 3:26-cv-03130). A notice from the firm Federman & Sherwood, published on Business Wire, described it as a securities class action against PAH, both REITs and Nelson on behalf of investors who bought between March 2022 and July 2024. As of mid-November, the bankruptcy docket showed a November 24, 2026 hearing set on the debtors' cash collateral, cash management and automatic-stay motions.

timeline.label: The REITs' management agreements with Phoenix American Hospitality end
SEC files a settled action against Phoenix American Hospitality and its president; judgments entered June 5
Proven Business Skills Inc sues Phoenix American Hospitality in N.D. Texas; a class action notice also names both REITs
The REIT, REIT II and 14 affiliates file Chapter 11 in the N.D. Texas bankruptcy court
